request_state.conjecture: Beal: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and gcd(gcd(A,B),C) = 1 has no solutions. Audit has shown three recurring failure modes in this project: conflating a residual mod-p congruence with an isogeny or l-adic statement; using a Chabauty rank bound over a base field to conclude about points of higher degree; and relabelling a GRH-conditional or heuristic result as unconditional.

candidate_A.claim: TESTED AND REFUTED: the shortcut round the opposite-parity (3,4,4) branch that would avoid Euler's theorem. Besides mu^6+nu^6 = 2 tau^3, the descent also yields tau^3 + (mu nu)^3 = 2C^2 and tau^3 - (mu nu)^3 = 2B^2, since tau^3 = C^2+B^2 and (mu nu)^3 = C^2-B^2. If either of x^3 +/- y^3 = 2z^2 forced x = y, the branch would close with no Euler input. Neither does.
candidate_A.method: Exact search, no floating point. x^3+y^3 = 2z^2 with coprime x > y has at least 10 solutions below 3000, smallest (13,11,42) and (23,1,78); x^3-y^3 = 2z^2 has at least 18, smallest (5,3,7). Verified exactly: 13^3+11^3 = 2*42^2, 23^3+1^3 = 2*78^2, 5^3-3^3 = 2*7^2.
candidate_A.failure_reason: The square-target variants have abundant coprime solutions with x != y, so they impose no constraint. The cube on the right-hand side of a^3+b^3 = 2c^3 is doing the work, not the factor 2 or the sum-of-cubes shape. Euler's theorem is genuinely the needed input and cannot be traded for a weaker cousin.
candidate_A.obligations: Extracted lemma, preserved for reuse: when a descent produces several simultaneous conditions, check each candidate closure separately -- shapes that look equally strong can differ completely in solvability. Recorded as a permanent assertion in code/U320_regression_checks.py (check_u325_square_variants_are_dead) with positive witnesses, so the shortcut cannot be proposed again without the counterexamples surfacing.
candidate_A.novelty: A negative result that sharpens C177: it explains WHY the (3,4,4) chain needs Euler specifically. Cost: one cheap exact search. Nothing about Beal's open core.

evaluations.U325: Exact search with explicit verified witnesses. HYPOTHESIS_ONLY for routing.

inspirations: asking where the technique that worked on (3,4,4) can apply at all, before reusing it
candidate_B.evidence: The smallest open signatures all have pairwise gcds (1,1,1): (3,5,7), (4,5,7), (3,4,11), (5,7,11).
candidate_B.failure_reason: The open core is precisely the set of signatures with pairwise DISTINCT reduced exponents — (4,q,r) with q,r distinct odd primes, and (p,q,r) odd primes not all equal — so the descent NEVER applies there. This is a structural reason, not a failure of effort.
candidate_B.claim: THE SCOPE OF THE (3,4,4) DESCENT, exactly. That descent needed C^z - B^y to FACTOR, which requires gcd(y,z) > 1. Among reduced exponents — 4 or odd primes — two of them have gcd exceeding 1 ONLY WHEN THEY ARE EQUAL (verified: no pair (a,b) of distinct reduced exponents has gcd > 1). So the technique applies exactly to signatures with a REPEATED exponent: (3,4,4), (p,p,r), (n,n,n) and the like. Of 219 reduced hyperbolic signatures with exponents in {4} union the odd primes up to 29, 99 admit a factorisation and 120 do not.
candidate_B.method: exact enumeration over reduced hyperbolic signatures; gcd computation
candidate_B.extracted_lemma: Factorisation-based descent is available exactly when two exponents coincide. That is the same boundary the rest of this session found by other means: C128 (a rigid object carries at most two exponents), C131 and C136 (classical Frey models absorb only the pairs (2,3) and (n,n)), and C157 here. Three independent lines all stop at the same place — two exponents may be related, the third may not.
candidate_B.novelty: This ties the (3,4,4) work back to the general obstruction. The descent was not a new route to Beal: it was available precisely because (3,4,4) has a repeated exponent, which is exactly the configuration the open core excludes.

compatible.instructions: Are these two research candidates mathematically COMPATIBLE, in the sense that the objects, fields, exponents and equations they concern are the same or are related by a reduction that the project has already proved?

criteria.true: they concern the same equation, signature, curve or field, or one supplies an input the other consumes
criteria.false: they concern unrelated equations, signatures or methods, so no joint statement could be formed without inventing a new reduction

combination_value.instructions: If these two candidates were combined into a single line of attack, how much would the combination accomplish beyond what the better of the two accomplishes alone?
criteria: level 0: nothing; the combination is just the stronger candidate restated, or they are incompatible
level 1: the combination tidies bookkeeping but resolves no obligation that either one leaves open
level 2: one candidate discharges a specific open obligation recorded in the other
level 3: the combination closes a case or an infinite family that neither one closes alone

shared_failure.instructions: Would these two candidates FAIL FOR THE SAME REASON, so that combining them adds no diversity of failure mechanism and a single obstruction would defeat both?

criteria.true: both depend on the same blocked step, the same unverified citation, or the same one of the three recorded failure modes
criteria.false: they would fail for different reasons, so each provides genuine independent information
